findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Observed a container of open milk and corn salsa to be held past date marking maximum. Discussed with PIC, education was provided on proper date marking practices. Milk and corn were both discarded, ensure any TCS item is discarded after its 7 day date marking maximum.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

findings.title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
findings.comment: Observed plates to not be inverted at the service station. DIscussed with PIC, education was provided and plates were inverted. Ensure any clean plates are stored in a way that prevents any possible contamination.
findings.citation_text: 4-903.11(B) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (B) Clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS shall be stored as specified under (A) of this section and shall be stored: (1) In a self-draining position that allows air drying; and (2) Covered or inverted.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Observed kitchen prep cooler 1 to be soiled with food debris/mold. Discussed with PIC, prep cooler will be cleaned. Ensure prep coolers are being cleaned at a frequency that prevents food/mold build up.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Observed raw fish to be stored next to raw chicken in kitchen line prep cooler. Discussed with PIC, education was provided on proper storage order, fish was moved to a location above chicken. Ensure facility is following proper storage order to prevent any possible cross-contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(2) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (2) Except when combined as ingredients, separating types of raw animal FOODS from each other such as beef, FISH, lamb, pork, and POULTRY during storage, preparation, holding, and display by: (a) Using separate EQUIPMENT for each type, or (b) Arranging each type of FOOD in EQUIPMENT so that cross contamination of one type with another is prevented, and (c) Preparing each type of FOOD at different times or in separate areas.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed small amounts of black mold to be present at ice machine. Discussed with PIC, ice machine will be emptied and cleaned. Ensure staff is cleaning ice machine at a frequency that prevents mold accumulation.

findings.comment: Observed a container of open milk and cheese to not have any date marking available. Discussed with PIC, education was provided on proper date marking practices. Milk and cheese were both discarded, ensure any TCS item that is kept longer than 24 hours is properly date marked.

findings.title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
findings.comment: Observed the walk in cooler to not have a working thermometer present. A thermometer was in the walk in cooler, however it was not working. Discussed with PIC, the broken thermometer was replaced with a working one. Ensure a working thermometer is available in all coolers during all hours of operation.
findings.citation_text: 4-204.112(D) Temperature Measuring Devices. (D) TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be designed to be easily readable.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.comment:
Observed the following items to be stored on the floor:
1) A bag of flour was observed to be resting on the floor in the prep/dish machine room. 
2) A container holding beef was observed to be resting on the floor in back walk in cooler. 
3) A container holding s’mores supplies was observed to be resting on the floor in bar. 

Discussed with PIC, education was provided on proper location for storing foods. All items were relocated to at least 6 inches off of ground. Ensure any food item is kept at least 6 inches off of ground to prevent any possible contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
findings.comment: Observed multiple knives on knife rack to be soiled with food debris. Discussed with PIC, knives were removed and put through wash, rinse, and sanitize location. Ensure knives are properly cleaned before being placed on knife rack.
findings.citation_text: 4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

findings.citation_text: 6-303.11(A) Intensity. The light intensity shall be: (A) At least 108 lux (10 foot candles) at a distance of 75 cm (30 inches) above the floor, in walk-in refrigeration units and dry FOOD storage areas and in other areas and rooms during periods of cleaning;

findings.title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
findings.comment:
Observed no allergen training to have been completed by any CFM’s available during inspection. Discussed with PIC, allergen training will be completed. Ensure all CFM’s have completed the required allergen training. 

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Observed kitchen line ice bath to be cold holding chicken at 47F. Discussed with PIC, education was provided on proper ice baths and water was added to the ice. Inspector observed chicken to later be at 41F. Ensure all ice baths are properly cold holding any TCS food at or below 41F.
